uncited: *   **Input:** Voxel grid position (`xyz`), voxel size, ray direction (`direction`), and an initial offset (`offset`) derived from the voxel position.
*   `offset`: A vector representing the displacement from the voxel center to the ray start point (often half-voxel or zero depending on the specific voxelization scheme).
Apply the jitter to the components of `r_origin` that are perpendicular to the ray direction.
*   If `direction` is 0 (X-ray), jitter is applied to Y and Z components.
*   If `direction` is 1 (Y-ray), jitter is applied to X and Z components.
*   If `direction` is 2 (Z-ray), jitter is applied to X and Y components.
The jitter calculation adds a constant number of arithmetic operations and comparisons to the existing voxelization loop.
No new data structures are required; the jitter is computed on the fly.
*   Only addresses coplanarity issues related to ray origins.
*   Requires knowledge of the ray direction and voxel size.
*   **When to use:** Use this method when voxelizing STL meshes (especially terrain/heightmap data) using ray-triangle intersection and observing vertical gaps or missing voxels.
*   **When not to use:** If the mesh is highly irregular or if the voxelization pipeline already uses a robust intersection algorithm with epsilon handling, this may be unnecessary.
